title: Aude Diagnostics – Internal Data-Integrity Dashboard
summary: An internal diagnostics web app that reads straight from the database, verifies the main product is producing correct data for every client, and puts the health of all of them on one screen built for troubleshooting.
overview: Aude's main application generates data for many clients, and the team had no single place to confirm that data was correct for all of them at once.

I built a separate internal web application that talks directly to the database, checks the main app's output per client, and surfaces the results in one dashboard aimed squarely at the engineers who debug it.
problem: There was no fast way to tell whether the main application was generating correct data across every client, so verifying an issue meant checking clients one at a time.
solution: A dedicated diagnostics dashboard that reads from the database directly, evaluates per-client data integrity, and presents the whole picture in a layout designed for troubleshooting rather than for general reporting.

howItWorks.title: Direct database checks
howItWorks.description: The app queries the database directly and evaluates whether the main application is producing correct data for each client.

howItWorks.title: One-glance dashboard
howItWorks.description: Results for every client are laid out so an engineer can see what is not working without drilling in first. The UI is designed for troubleshooting, not general reporting.

howItWorks.title: Shareable deep links
howItWorks.description: Engineers can explore down to a cause and share a URL that reopens exactly the view they were looking at, so a finding travels with a link instead of a screenshot.

howItWorks.title: User's-eye view
howItWorks.description: A view that shows the UI as the end user sees it alongside the API response behind it, so a visual symptom can be traced to the payload that caused it.

buildingProcess.title: Learning the existing product
buildingProcess.description: Started by exploring the existing Aude web application and fixing bugs in it, mostly on the UI, which built up the understanding of the data flows the diagnostics tool would later have to verify.

buildingProcess.title: Building the diagnostics app
buildingProcess.description: Built the dashboard as a separate application talking directly to the database, and shaped the interface around how engineers actually debug: broad status first, then drill-down, then a shareable link.

buildingProcess.title: Deploying behind the existing authentication
buildingProcess.description: Deployed to AWS EC2 and served it from the same domain as the main application so it could reuse the existing PropelAuth session instead of introducing a second authentication system.

challenges.challenge: Reusing the main product's PropelAuth authentication for a second, separately deployed application, which PropelAuth does not support natively.
challenges.solution: Deployed the app on AWS EC2 and routed a dedicated path on the main application's existing load balancer to the new target group, so both applications are served from one domain and share the same session. The app checks for a valid session and redirects to the existing login UI when there is none.
challenges.lesson: Sharing an origin can be a legitimate architectural answer to an authentication constraint, rather than reaching for a second identity system.

challenges.challenge: The dashboard exposes internal data, so being logged in is not sufficient authorization.
challenges.solution: Layered a second check on top of the session: a user must belong to the organization and hold a specific role before the diagnostics app will serve them, keeping access limited to the intended engineers.
challenges.lesson: Authentication and authorization are separate problems, and internal tooling needs both.

features: Per-client data-integrity checks read directly from the database
Troubleshooting-first dashboard showing failures at a glance
Deep linking so a specific investigation can be shared as a URL
User's-eye UI view paired with the API response behind it
Role-restricted access on top of the existing single sign-on
highlights: Built an internal diagnostics dashboard that verifies per-client data integrity straight from the database.
Designed the interface for engineers: failures visible at a glance, deep-linkable investigations, and a user's-eye view paired with its API response.
Deployed on AWS EC2 behind the main application's existing load balancer so it reuses the existing single sign-on, with an additional role check restricting access.
lessonsLearned: How to design an interface around a debugging workflow instead of around the data model.
That deep-linkable state turns an investigation into something a team can share and reproduce.
How routing and shared origins can solve an authentication constraint without adding a second identity system.
